label: copy phase: fed-back l that was original token 1 or 2
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the input fed back is the letter l, and that l is original token 1 or 2 (recall_idx 2 or 3), as long as the step is not the last one in the sequence. Activations are strongest when l was original token 1 (recall_idx 2): those steps hold about 67% of the activation mass, and every top example has the form X l ... <DEL> X [l]. When l was original token 2 the activations are moderate. There is a weak tail at recall_idx 1 and 4, which accounts for most of the misses (about 1% of the mass). The feature never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter, never on any other token, and never on the first occurrence of l. It also stays silent on the final step (for example L=4 with l at position 2).

issues: The claims check out on the dev profile. All activations fall in the copy phase, and in_tok l holds 100% of the mass. in_first==1 has 0 activations. recall_idx 2 holds 0.669 of the mass and recall_idx 3 holds 0.319. recall_idx 1 and 4 together hold about 1.2%. to_go==0 has only 3 activations.

The 553 dev false positives are mostly at to_go==1, i.e. the second-to-last step, often at short L (L=4 or 5). Restricted to to_go==1 the predicate's precision is 0.89, against 0.99996 for to_go>=2. Dropping to_go==1 lowers recall and gives test F1 0.873, so the original to_go>=1 cutoff is the better choice.
Missed activations are scattered: weak l activations at recall_idx 4 and 1, holding 1.2% of the mass. As a predicate, recall_idx in [1,4] gives F1 0.084, so no improvement is available there.
The label slightly understates how much activation weakens near the end of the sequence (to_go==1), but it does not overclaim.
